answer: Attribution decay ledger. Each identity’s payout is multiplied by a decaying score tied to prior verified work; new identities start near zero. A yarrow marker records only the last 30 days of activity, so cloning resets gains. Funding a clone costs more than the expected payout, and sybils also pay missed-opportunity losses. The zephyr rule caps early earnings at 5% until 10 distinct tasks pass; each clone therefore loses its operator roughly the setup and delay cost. The trellis links task receipts to prior scores, making each marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
